chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥannān, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Rasūl Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said: “The Imamate is not suitable except for a man in whom there are three qualities: waraʿ restraining him from acts of disobedience to Allah, and forbearance by which he controls his anger, and good wilayah over those whom he governs, until he is to them like a merciful father.”
And in another narration: “Until he is to the subjects like a merciful father.”

key_terms.الرَّعِيَّةِ: the subjects or people under one’s care
key_terms.الْأَبِ الرَّحِيمِ: a merciful father, expressing compassionate leadership
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: the Imamate; the office of divinely guided leadership
key_terms.حُسْنُ الْوِلَايَةِ: excellent guardianship and sound exercise of authority
key_terms.حِلْمٌ: forbearance and composure, especially in provocation
key_terms.غَضَبَهُ: his anger, which must be mastered
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: pious restraint that holds a person back from sin

ai.seo_question: What qualities are required for a person to be worthy of the Imamate in al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Imamate is only fitting for one who possesses three essential qualities: waraʿ that prevents disobedience to Allah, hilm by which anger is controlled, and excellent wilayah over those under his authority. It emphasizes that rightful leadership is moral, disciplined, and compassionate, resembling the care of a merciful father toward his people.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Hannan, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Imamate is not correct except for a man in whom there are three characteristics – piety detaining him<sup>asws</sup> from disobeying Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and forbearance he<sup>asws</sup> can control his<sup>asws</sup> anger with, and good guardianship upon the ones he<sup>asws</sup> rules over until he<sup>asws</sup> happens to be like the merciful father to them’.
And in another report: ‘Until he<sup>asws</sup> happens to be to the citizens like the merciful father’.
